lean.statement:
theorem result
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (P : Measure (E × ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (hGaussian : P.map Prod.fst = ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E)
    (p : Polynomial ℝ)
    (hlabel : MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => z.2) 2 P) :
    let U := {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}
    let predictor : Measure U → E → ℝ := fun rho x => ∫ w : U, p.eval ⟪w.1,x⟫_ℝ ∂rho
    let risk : Measure U → ℝ := fun rho => ∫ z, (predictor rho z.1 - z.2)^2 ∂P
    let potential : Measure U → U → ℝ := fun rho w =>
      2 * ∫ z, (predictor rho z.1 - z.2) * p.eval ⟪w.1,z.1⟫_ℝ ∂P
    (∀ rho : Measure U, IsProbabilityMeasure rho →
      Integrable (fun z : E × ℝ => (predictor rho z.1 - z.2)^2) P ∧
      ∀ w : U, Integrable (fun z : E × ℝ =>
        (predictor rho z.1 - z.2) * p.eval ⟪w.1,z.1⟫_ℝ) P) ∧
    ∀ rho0 rho1 : Measure U, IsProbabilityMeasure rho0 → IsProbabilityMeasure rho1 →
      let curve : ℝ → Measure U := fun t =>
        ENNReal.ofReal (1-t) • rho0 + ENNReal.ofReal t • rho1
      Integrable (potential rho0) rho0 ∧ Integrable (potential rho0) rho1 ∧
      HasDerivWithinAt (fun t => risk (curve t))
        ((∫ w, potential rho0 w ∂rho1) - (∫ w, potential rho0 w ∂rho0))
        (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) 0 ∧
      risk rho0 + ((∫ w, potential rho0 w ∂rho1) - (∫ w, potential rho0 w ∂rho0)) ≤
        risk rho1
approved_definition_context: MemLp f 2 mu means that the displayed scalar function is almost-everywhere strongly measurable and has finite L2 seminorm under mu. IsProbabilityMeasure rho means rho has total mass one.

The subtype {w : E // norm w = 1} has the subspace topology and induced Borel measurable structure inherited from E. stdGaussian E is the standard centered Gaussian measure with identity covariance on the finite-dimensional real inner-product space. P.map Prod.fst is the actual first-coordinate pushforward of the joint law P.

Every displayed integral is the actual real Bochner integral. This operator is totalized outside its integrable domain; Integrable f mu explicitly certifies almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the norm.

ENNReal.ofReal embeds the maximum of the real argument and zero into the nonnegative extended reals; the measure scaling and addition are the literal positive-measure operations. HasDerivWithinAt f d S a asserts a derivative of f with value d at a within S, using the actual value f(a).
